reason: E1 and E2 support that high configurational entropy can stabilize solid solutions in bulk HEAs, but E2 warns that ordering enthalpy may overcome entropy at low temperatures, and none of the cited evidence addresses nanoparticle-specific stability or the full temperature range up to 1923 K. premises: High configurational entropy reduces free energy of solid-solution phases, especially at high temperatures.
This entropy stabilization prevents phase segregation or chemical ordering.
The effect applies to nanoparticles with five or more metals in equal/near-equal ratios.
